Hi Olivia — thanks, and great question.

Attached is a first-draft set of snippets (short and console-sized) that you can drop into the questionnaire and the account settings UI. I kept the language simple and actionable. Before I send to you as "final," legal (Kimberly) will review for accuracy and any legal-y wording.

Draft short blurb for procurement (3 bullets):
- Processing locations: We operate servers and partner data centers in North America, EU, and APAC; some processing may occur in other regions to optimize latency.
- Subprocessors: We work with a limited set of subprocessors (cloud providers, monitoring, and storage). The current list is published and kept up to date here: [link to subprocessor CSV].
- Transfers & safeguards: When data is transferred across borders, we apply contractual safeguards (Standard Contractual Clauses where required), and customers can use features like dedicated key management to control encryption keys.

Console one-liner (for account settings):
"Your data may be processed in NA, EU, and APAC. See our subprocessors and transfer safeguards for details."

Jonas — thanks for the clear draft. A few edits and a suggested final copy below. The goal is to minimize ambiguity while staying digestible for procurement and sales.

Edits / guidance:
- Replace "may be processed" with "is processed" where we know locations, and "may be processed" only where routing or caching could push work to other regions. Avoid suggesting blanket global transfers.
- Be explicit that the subprocessor list is maintained and includes locations for each subprocessor — link to CSV is good.
- For transfers: say we rely on contractual safeguards (SCCs) and technical controls (encryption at rest/in transit, customer-managed keys as an option). Do not use the word "guarantee".
- Console one-liner should point to a more detailed page; avoid listing regions in the one-liner if it makes it too long.

Suggested procurement blurb — tuned for legal review (3 short bullets):
- Where we process data: Primary processing occurs in the United States, European Union, and APAC regions. Requests may be routed to nearby regions for performance; we document regional processing in our subprocessor map.
- Subprocessors: We engage subprocessors for cloud hosting, observability, and storage. Our published subprocessor list (updated monthly) shows each provider and the regions they operate in: https://drive.redwood.company/drive/folders/1a2b3c-subprocessor-evidence
- Transfers & safeguards: Cross-border transfers are covered by contractual safeguards (Standard Contractual Clauses where required) and technical controls such as TLS and encryption at rest. Customers can opt for customer-managed keys (KMS) to control encryption keys.

Suggested console one-liner (short, links to details):
"We process data in select regions. See subprocessors & transfer safeguards for details."

Kim — please confirm the above is accurate from your side, and I'll mark this as legal-reviewed if ok. I also attached a CSV export of the current subprocessor list for procurement: redwood-subprocessor-list-20271104.csv

Regards,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-subprocessor-list-20271104.csv (text/csv)
